text: Now a man named Ananias, together with his wife Sapphira, sold a piece of property.
With his wife's knowledge he held back part of the price, and brought only a portion of it and laid it at the apostles' feet.
But Peter said, "Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart, that you should lie to the Holy Spirit and hold back part of the price of the land?
While it remained unsold, was it not your own? And after it was sold, was the money not at your disposal? Why have you contrived this thing in your heart? You have not lied to men but to God."
When Ananias heard these words, he fell down and died. And great fear came over all who heard of it.
The young men rose, wrapped him up, carried him out, and buried him.
About three hours later his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
Peter said to her, "Tell me, was this the price you got for the land?" "Yes," she said, "that was the price."
Then Peter said to her, "How could you agree together to put the Spirit of the Lord to the test? Look, the feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out."
At once she fell down at his feet and died. When the young men came in, they found her dead, and they carried her out and buried her beside her husband.
And great fear came over the whole church and over all who heard of these things.
Many signs and wonders were done among the people through the hands of the apostles, and they all met together with one accord in Solomon's Colonnade.
None of the others dared to join them, but the people held them in high esteem.
And more than ever, believers were added to the Lord—great numbers of both men and women—

versions.text: And still more came to believe in the Lord, great numbers of both men and women,
versions.explanation: The Greek says believers were "added to the Lord" (προσετίθεντο), which conveys their being joined to the Lord and his community, not merely that more people believed. Restoring this keeps the sense of growth in the church that ties back to verses 12–13.

text: so that they even carried the sick out into the streets and laid them on cots and mats, hoping that as Peter came by at least his shadow might fall on one of them.
Crowds also gathered from the towns around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those tormented by unclean spirits, and all of them were healed.
Then the high priest and all who were with him, that is, the party of the Sadducees, rose up, filled with jealousy.
They arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail.
But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison, led them out, and said,
"Go, stand in the temple and tell the people the whole message of this life."

So at daybreak they entered the temple and began to teach. Meanwhile the high priest and those with him arrived, called together the Council—the full assembly of the elders of Israel—and sent to the jail to have the apostles brought in.
But when the officers arrived, they did not find them in the prison, so they went back and reported,
"We found the jail securely locked and the guards standing at the doors, but when we opened them, we found no one inside."
When the captain of the temple guard and the chief priests heard this, they were at a loss, wondering what would come of it.
Then someone came and reported to them, "Look, the men you put in prison are standing in the temple, teaching the people!"
So the captain went with his officers and brought them in—without force, for they were afraid the people would stone them.
They brought them in and made them stand before the Council, and the high priest questioned them:
"We gave you strict orders not to teach in this name. Yet you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you intend to bring this man's blood upon us."
Peter and the apostles answered, "We must obey God rather than men.
The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you killed by hanging him on a tree.
God exalted him to his right hand as Prince and Savior, to grant repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.

versions.text: God exalted him to his right hand as Author of life and Savior, to grant repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.
versions.explanation: The Greek here reads simply ἀρχηγόν ("leader," "prince," "pioneer"), without the qualifier "of life" (that phrase, ἀρχηγὸν τῆς ζωῆς, occurs in 3:15). "Author of life" adds content not present in this verse.

text: We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him."
When they heard this, they were furious and wanted to put them to death.
But a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law who was respected by all the people, stood up in the Council and ordered that the men be taken outside for a little while.
Then he said, "Men of Israel, be careful what you intend to do with these men.
Some time ago Theudas appeared, claiming to be somebody, and about four hundred men joined him. He was killed, and all who followed him were dispersed and came to nothing.

versions.text: Some time ago Theudas appeared, claiming to be somebody, and about four hundred men joined him. He was killed, and all who followed him were scattered and came to nothing.
versions.explanation: Verse 36 uses διελύθησαν ("broken up, dispersed") while verse 37 uses διεσκορπίσθησαν ("scattered"). Using a different verb here preserves the distinction and avoids the repetitive echo when the two verses are read aloud together.

text: After him Judas the Galilean appeared in the days of the census and drew people after him. He too perished, and all who followed him were scattered.
So in this case I tell you: keep away from these men and let them alone. For if this plan or this work is of human origin, it will collapse;
but if it is from God, you will not be able to stop them. You may even find yourselves fighting against God." They were persuaded by him,
and they called in the apostles, had them flogged, ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.
So they left the Council rejoicing that they had been counted worthy to suffer dishonor for the Name.
And every day, in the temple and from house to house, they never stopped teaching and proclaiming the good news that Jesus is the Christ.
